definitions.explanation: The daughter of one's brother or sister. The 〜っ{子|こ} ending makes it warmer than plain {姪|めい}, and it is the everyday spoken form.

examples.japanese: {姪|めい}っ{子|こ}は{三歳|さんさい}だ。
examples.english: My niece is three years old.

examples.japanese: {姪|めい}っ{子|こ}の{入学式|にゅうがくしき}の{写真|しゃしん}が{届|とど}いた。
examples.english: Photos from my niece's school entrance ceremony arrived.

examples.japanese: {久|ひさ}しぶりに{会|あ}った{姪|めい}っ{子|こ}は、すっかり{大|おお}きくなっていた。
examples.english: My niece, whom I hadn't seen in a long time, had grown up completely.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {姪|めい}っ{子|こ}が{生|う}まれる: to have a niece born
- {姪|めい}っ{子|こ}をかわいがる: to dote on one's niece
- {姪|めい}っ{子|こ}と{甥|おい}っ{子|こ}: one's nieces and nephews

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {姪|めい}: niece — the plain, neutral term used in writing and formal contexts
- {甥|おい}っ{子|こ}: nephew — the matching form
- いとこ: cousin — a different relation that learners often mix up with {姪|めい}

Japanese has no single word covering both nieces and nephews, so speakers say {甥|おい}っ{子|こ}{姪|めい}っ{子|こ} when they mean the pair together.
